what-is-budojo.question: What is Budojo?
what-is-budojo.answer: It runs your martial-arts academy — BJJ, judo, karate or taekwondo — from this computer: athletes, attendance, fees, documents, timetable and programme in one place. It is not an online service — your data stays on your machine, and Budojo works with no connection at all.

create-academy.question: How do I start?
create-academy.answer: The first time you open it you create your sign-in, and Budojo walks you through a short setup: the martial art you teach, the academy's name, the days you train, done. There is no email to confirm — the sign-in belongs to this computer. Everything in there can be changed later from Academy → Edit — the martial art until the academy has athletes, a timetable or a programme.

invite-coach.question: Can I give a second instructor access?
invite-coach.answer: Not yet. Budojo is built for one person on one computer: there is no server for a second instructor to connect to. If you need it, say so from More → Contact support — requests are queued by real demand.

add-athlete.question: How do I add an athlete?
add-athlete.answer: Open Athletes and press Add athlete, top right. Name, belt, status and the date they joined: only the name is genuinely required, the rest you fill in when you know it. Save, and they are on the list.

import-athletes.question: How do I bring in the list I already keep in a spreadsheet?
import-athletes.answer: Athletes → Import. Pick a CSV with a header row: Budojo reads the columns — first name, surname, belt, stripes, status, joined on, email, phone, date of birth — and shows you how it read them, so you can fix anything before importing. Coming from Excel: File → Save as → CSV. Semicolons, accents and day-first dates are already handled.

belt-not-listed.question: My belt is not in the list. What now?
belt-not-listed.answer: The belts come from the martial art the academy teaches: the IBJJF scale for BJJ (grey to green for the kids, white to black with up to 6 degrees, then coral and red), the FIJLKAM kyu, half-belts and dan for judo and karate, the WT kup, half-belts, poom and dan for taekwondo. A missing belt usually means the academy was set up with another martial art: you can change it from Academy → Edit until the academy has athletes, a timetable or a programme. If your school uses a scale none of these match, say so from More → Contact support.

suspend-athlete.question: How do I pause someone who has stopped for a while?
suspend-athlete.answer: Open the athlete, go to Edit and set Status to Inactive. They stay in the archive with their whole attendance and payment history, but drop out of the check-in and out of who needs chasing. The eye in the list's filter row brings them back into view when you need them; set them back to Active when they return to the mat.

mark-attendance.question: How do I take attendance?
mark-attendance.answer: Open Attendance: it is tonight's check-in. The classes for the day sit at the top with their times, already on the nearest one; pick whoever is on the mat and the row lights up. It saves itself, and if you get one wrong there is an Undo in the message that appears.

edit-attendance.question: Can I fix attendance for a past day?
edit-attendance.answer: Yes: change the date at the top and correct it there. No window closes on you. If nobody trains today, Budojo opens the last session that ran and says so at the top of the page.

attendance-summary.question: Where do I see how often each of them came this month?
attendance-summary.answer: Attendance → Monthly summary: one row per athlete with days trained, days available and the rate, sorted by who comes most. The arrows beside the month move you back and forward.

timetable.question: Where do I set the class times?
timetable.answer: Academy → Timetable. Each class has a day, time, length and kind — gi or no-gi, kata or kumite, as your martial art splits it — and the whole week reads in one screen. This is how the check-in knows which classes run tonight, and it is where the academy's training days come from.

programme.question: What is the Programme for?
programme.answer: Academy → Programme is the list of positions and techniques you teach. The “in season” tick says what you are covering this year: it is the denominator coverage does its arithmetic against. Starting from nothing, Budojo offers the full programme of your martial art, where one has shipped, to start from and edit.

lesson-topics.question: How do I record what we worked on?
lesson-topics.answer: In the check-in, under the day's classes, there is the topics row: Add topics opens the lesson sheet. Search a technique, take a suggestion (it tells you why it is suggesting it) or walk the programme, then save. The same sheet opens from the Timetable on a class's own button, if you would rather plan the next one than write up the one just finished.

coverage.question: How do I know what I have not taught yet?
coverage.answer: Stats → Programme: how many in-season techniques you have actually done, broken down by position, which ones you touched only once, which you have not done at all, and when each was last taught. Every athlete then has their own Coverage tab, saying what they missed.

set-monthly-fee.question: How do I set the monthly fee?
set-monthly-fee.answer: Academy → Edit, the Monthly fee field. From then on each athlete's Payments tab and the mark-as-paid control in the list switch on. If you do not run payments here, leave it empty: both controls simply stay away.

fee-tiers.question: What if they do not all pay the same?
fee-tiers.answer: The same page carries the Monthly price list: create the tiers you need — twice a week, unlimited, reduced — with a name and an amount, then set an athlete's tier on their own page. Anyone without a tier pays the academy's monthly fee.

mark-paid.question: How do I mark someone as paid?
mark-paid.answer: Two ways. From the athlete list, the payment chip on their row records the current month. From the athlete's page, Payments shows the year month by month: that is where you record back months and longer periods (quarterly, yearly).

unpaid-badge.question: What does the “Unpaid” chip mean?
unpaid-badge.answer: That nothing pays for this athlete's current month: no fee payment covers it, and they hold no carnet with entries left. To see everyone to chase, press the Payment button above the list until it reads Unpaid — on a phone, until its icon is a circle with an X. Athletes with a carnet still in use, inactive athletes, athletes charged no fee and your own row never appear there.

carnets.question: How do I handle class passes?
carnets.answer: Set the price and how many entries a pass carries in Academy → Edit, then sell one from the athlete's Payments tab: from there on every attendance takes an entry off it and the card tells you how many are left. If you count one entry per day rather than per class, that option sits next to the price.

upload-medical-cert.question: How do I upload a medical certificate?
upload-medical-cert.answer: Open the athlete and go to Documents → Add document: pick the type (usually Medical certificate), set the issue and expiry dates and attach the PDF or photo. The expiry date is what drives the warnings, so it is worth getting right.

expiring-documents.question: Where do I see every certificate that needs renewing?
expiring-documents.answer: The warning triangle in the athlete list's filter row carries the count of who has no certificate and whose is running out; opening it lands on the full list — first the ones missing entirely, then the ones expiring — each linking straight to that athlete's documents. When it is grey there is nothing to do.

backup.question: How do I back up?
backup.answer: More → Backup (the page is called Data & backup). Budojo writes an archive by itself every six hours while it is open, and Back up now makes one immediately. A backup that only lives on this computer's disk does not survive that disk, though: also pick a folder — one your cloud already syncs, a network drive, a USB stick — or connect Google Drive, and every archive is copied there for you.

restore-backup.question: How do I put the data back from a backup?
restore-backup.answer: On the same page, every archive in the list has a Restore: it replaces what you have now with what is in the archive, and asks before it does. On a new computer it takes two things, in either order: restoring the archive, and importing your recovery keys — without the keys the documents inside the archive will not open.

recovery-code.question: What is the recovery code?
recovery-code.answer: It is the key that opens the documents kept inside your backups. Find it under Backup → Recovery keys → Reveal recovery code: put it in a password manager and never share it, because anyone holding it can read those documents. On a fresh installation you paste it into “Restore keys from a recovery code”, and Budojo restarts to apply them.

where-is-my-data.question: Where is my data?
where-is-my-data.answer: On this computer, in Budojo's data folder — “%APPDATA%\Budojo” on Windows — together with the documents you upload and the backup archives. Nothing leaves the machine unless you copy it there yourself (the backup folder, or Google Drive). Uninstalling Budojo does not touch that folder: the data stays.

update-budojo.question: How do I update Budojo?
update-budojo.answer: It updates itself: when a new version is out the title bar at the top says so and the download starts on its own. Install puts it on straight away; do nothing and it installs the next time you close Budojo. What changed is in What's new, in the sidebar.

change-language.question: How do I change the language?
change-language.answer: More → Language, then pick Italian or English: the whole app — pages, forms, menus, messages — switches at once. The choice sticks after you close and reopen Budojo.

export-data.question: How do I download a copy of my data?
export-data.answer: More → Settings → Account → Download my data: you get a ZIP with the academy, athletes, payments, attendance and uploaded documents, readable in any ordinary software. If what you want is a copy you can put back into Budojo, that is the backup instead.

delete-account.question: How do I delete everything?
delete-account.answer: There is no account on a server to close: the data is here. Uninstall Budojo and delete the data folder (“%APPDATA%\Budojo” on Windows), plus any archives you copied elsewhere — backup folder or Google Drive. If there is any chance you will want it back, take a backup first and keep it somewhere safe.

summary.method: Here an attendance is one athlete's day of training: an evening with two lessons counts once for each athlete who was there, and the attendances above add up every athlete's days. The percentage divides an athlete's days by the month's training days in the timetable from the day they joined (or their first session, if earlier), up to today while the month is running, leaving out the days the academy was closed.
